newsitem.title: USA: US crude grades swing higher on expensive foreigns.
newsitem.headline: US crude grades swing higher on expensive foreigns.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices swung higher Tuesday morning for domestic grade barrels, supported by firming prices overseas making foreign barrels more costly.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing outright crude prices were some 25 cents higher at $20.00-10 a barrel in late morning dealings.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James barrels attracted deals at 24 cents over August WTI/Cushing, some 5-7 cents stronger than deals recorded on Monday.
Traders said the burgeoning strength in Dated Brent values supported sweet crudes, and helped bolster domestic grade barrels across the board.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold at $1.10 under August WTI, with a rumor that $1.08 sold as well, around 10 cents firmer than Monday.
"With Dated Brent trading at plus five cents, it is pushing the rest of the market higher," said a cash trader.
Other ranges talked in the grade markets saw Midland/WTI talk around a 25-30 cents discount to the marker, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire also at 20-25 cents below level.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus came in at a $1.96-2.00 range, seven cents stronger than Monday, reflecting the narrowing in the August/September spread to almost even.

August Exchange for Physicals were talked at only a two cents premium to the NYMEX screen. EFPs have continued to slide from lofty premiums in May and June, following the trimming of the foreign crude overhang in the U.S. Gulf. Refiners had propped EFPs as a security blanket against getting stuck with uneconomical foreign barrels.
